NOT in scope: the handoff relay (task-af9454f4's lane) or the evidence producer itself.

(2) PRODUCER SURFACE. `deriveReleaseTerminalEvidence(store, {attemptRef, projectId})` at release-terminal-evidence.ts:199. Evidence: {attemptRef, effectsTerminal, enumeratedEffects, enumeratedResources, nonTerminalEffectRefs, nonTerminalResourceRefs, ok, projectId, releasable, resourcesTerminal, terminalEffectRefs, terminalResourceRefs}. Refusal: {code, detail, layer:"RELEASE_TERMINAL_EVIDENCE", ok:false, upstream:{code,layer}|null}. `provenTerminal` = nonTerminal empty AND terminal non-empty. Zero-EFFECT unreachable (seeded from binding.effectIntentId); zero-RESOURCE reachable and answers FALSE at count 0 — the recorded choice, honored.

(3) CALL SITES. Production: foundation-attempt-service.ts:119 only (pins effectsTerminal:false/resourcesTerminal:false, and already calls recordTerminalEffect immediately above at :158). Everything else is attempt-release-disposition.test.ts. attempt-release-boundary.ts only NAMES it in prose.

(4) SUITE ARMS THIS ROW REPLACES: settledRequest literal :258-264 (both flags true); omitted sweep :436-457 (flags=[effectsTerminal,resourcesTerminal], driven===2); drained(flag) helper :823-832 + cardinality [2,1] and rows.length 3 at :846-853; and TWO two-call cases at :1106 and :1162 that use settledRequest({effectsTerminal:false}) so the FIRST call drains and the SECOND settles.

(5) FINDING — the two-call cases have an honest derived replacement. Unlike the safe boundary (one immutable committed run, cannot be upgraded between calls), terminal evidence is RE-READ live each call, so `recordTerminalEffect(store, {attemptRef, projectId})` BETWEEN the two calls flips effectsTerminal false->true. Fixture recipe validated against the producer suite's own seeds: derived-TRUE = OBSERVED run + recordTerminalEffect + applyAttemptResourceReport FAIL on the fenceable res-1 (fenceable FAIL -> RELEASED -> terminal); derived-FALSE-effects = skip recordTerminalEffect; derived-FALSE-resources = skip the fail (ACTIVE is non-terminal).

(6) FINDING — DRILL 5 (transposition) IS AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT AT THE kernelRequest SEAM, measured not assumed: lease-drain.ts:212 `settled = safeBoundaryObserved && effectsTerminal && resourcesTerminal` (a pure conjunction) and releaseRecordBody :139-167 records NEITHER flag, so swapping the two derived booleans changes no outcome and no durable byte. Mitigation planned instead of a vacuous drill: the shim returns a 2-key `flags` record that kernelRequest SPREADS, so no per-key write site exists at the seam, plus an asymmetric per-flag fixture pinning the shim's construction and a test asserting the flags record has EXACTLY those two keys (which is what keeps releaseWork's exact-seven-key contract). Residual will be disclosed in the completion.

(7) SCOPE NOTE — 8th file. attempt-release-store.ts must gain a FIFTH `AttemptReleaseLayer` member (ReleaseTerminalLayer) plus `ReleaseTerminalCode` in AttemptReleaseRefused["code"] and a `carryTerminalRefusal`, exactly as 78f38281 added the fourth layer + carryBoundaryRefusal there. Without it the passthrough refusal is untypeable. Not a producer; the carrier's own durable half. Plan listed 7 files; this makes 8, still under the 10 threshold.

WHAT THE SUITE NOW DRIVES.
(a) DERIVED-TRUE control — new "releases on the evidence the LEDGERS carry, with no terminality key sent": the producer's OWN answer for the fixture store is asserted [true,true] first, then the release is called with the four-key request and RELEASED is read back from durable bytes.
(b) DERIVED-FALSE — new "drains rather than releases when ONE enumerated item is not terminal" ([false,true] at the producer), plus the DRAINING family below.
(c) EVIDENCE-UNKNOWN BLOCKS — new "BLOCKS on an evidence UNKNOWN, carrying the producer's own code and layer": an undecodable terminal record planted at a MEASURED expectedVersion; both layers pinned; the carrier's refusal is compared against `deriveReleaseTerminalEvidence`'s own answer for the same store (code + upstream-as-message + layer) so neither side is an echo of the other, plus the literal RELEASE_TERMINAL_EFFECT_ENUMERATION_UNREADABLE and membership in RELEASE_TERMINAL_CODES; [durableRowCount, releaseDecisionCount] === [0,0] proves it lands before the kernel.
(d) CALLER FLAGS REFUSED — 2 keys x {true,false,"TERMINAL"} = driven 6 asserted, ATTEMPT_RELEASE_REQUEST_MALFORMED under DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RELEASE, no observation and no row. `true` is the AGREEING value for the fixture, which is the point.
(e) OMITTED SWEEP 2 -> 0. A zero-arm sweep passes vacuously, so the drop is asserted against the REQUEST rather than a hand-kept list: intersection of Object.keys(settledRequest()) with RETIRED_KEYS is [], the key set is EXACTLY [disposition,handoff,intentRefs,reason], and a positive control releases.
(f) PER-ARM TABLE. drained(flag) is gone. drainedBy(label,evidence,terminality,expected) asserts the producer's per-family answer for each arm's own store, then DRAINING: drainedByEffects [false,true], drainedByResources [true,false], drainedByBoundary [false,true] + the boundary's own recorded reason. Cardinality [1,1,1] and rows.length 3. The two deliberate-false cases (divergent-slot, draining-then-settled) were CONVERTED, not retired.

TWO MEASURED FACTS THE PLAN COULD NOT HAVE KNOWN.
1. The two-call cases have an honest derived route BECAUSE terminality is re-read every call: seed EFFECTS_PENDING, first call DRAINS, `terminaliseEffect(store)` between the calls, second call settles. The boundary could never do this (one committed run).
2. An UNOBSERVED run CANNOT carry a terminal effect — recordTerminalEffect answers EFFECT_TERMINAL_NOT_PROVEN because the ledger projects its settlement from the run. So every unobserved-boundary fixture necessarily has a pending effect; named UNOBSERVED_TERMINALITY, documented, and the boundary arm asserts SAFE_BOUNDARY_EXIT_UNOBSERVED so it stays distinguishable from the effects arm.

PRE-EXISTING FIXTURE BUG FIXED IN PASSING: the SLOT_REFUSALS it.each label `arm.name.slice(0,12)` carries whitespace and reaches a provider RUN REF; the settlement refuses it with PROVIDER_SETTLEMENT_RUN_REF_MALFORMED once a terminal effect is projected from that run. Slugged with a comment saying why.

plantedSlot also had to gain a real resource BIND (production `bindAttemptResources`, same writer the ingress drives): commitActivationLedgerRecord plants the activation alone, and an attempt holding no durable set is answered non-terminal at count 0, so every planted case would otherwise have drained for the wrong reason.
